newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber eases on sluggish Japanese orders.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber eases on sluggish Japanese orders.

text.p: Thai rubber prices eased this week on limited Japanese buying interest for near-term shipments and the absence of big Chinese forward orders, traders said on Friday.
They also said few exporters expected the Thai government to re-enter the domestic market to help boost local prices as expected earlier.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for October shipment eased to $1.24/kg FOB Bangkok from $1.28 last week. December/January delivery fell to $1.28/kg from $1.31-1.32.

Traders in the Hatyai market in southern Thailand said, however, that prices may firm next week as scattered daily rains in most southern provinces this week have prompted Thai smallholders to delay domestic sales in expectation of better prices.
They said moderate rains hit major rubber growing provinces including Trang, Surat Thani and Songkhla this week.
"Japanese buyers are already well stocked for September and October and they are now buying ahead for December and January," an exporter said.
